### What exists today

A working operational control tower for the ActiveHub order-to-provision journey:
configurable ingestion, a database-driven classification rule engine, dashboards,
operational queues, an order detail side panel with full rule trace and history, ingestion of
the daily downstream provisioning-failure report with ownership routing, an import history with
per-row error reporting, and an audit trail. It is deployed and in use.

### What this pack is for

To become the persisted specification record that drives future iterations of the platform,
and to make the gap between "delivered" and "certifiable" explicit and actionable.

## 2. Product Delivery Artefacts

### Epic

As an order operations team, we want a single control tower that ingests order data from the
systems that hold it, classifies every order line against rules we can change ourselves, and
surfaces the orders that need human action with a named owner for the next step — so that we
stop maintaining an Excel dashboard by hand, stop discovering customer-impacting provisioning
failures late, and can prove why any order was classified the way it was.

### Personas

| ID | Persona | Needs | Pain today |
|---|---|---|---|
| P-01 | Operations Analyst | See what needs working on now, in priority order; work a queue; see why an order is in it | Rebuilds an Excel view daily; no shared source of truth |
| P-02 | Operations Manager | Trend and mix over time; where the backlog is concentrated; whether it is getting better | No trend data; point-in-time snapshots only |
| P-03 | Order Management / Customer Data / ActiveHub Support / Platform Engineering (resolver teams) | To be told which failures are theirs and what the next step is | Failure emails are read by one person and forwarded ad hoc |
| P-04 | Control Tower Administrator | Add a data source and change classification rules without a code change or release | Logic lives in spreadsheet formulas known to one person |
| P-05 | Auditor / Reviewer | Evidence of what changed, when, by whom, and why an order was classified as it was | None |

### Acceptance Criteria (Given / When / Then)

**US-01 — Headline metrics**
- Given orders exist, when I open the dashboard, then I see counts for total, completed, pending, customer impacted, exceptions and cancelled.
- Given the summary request has not resolved, when the dashboard renders, then each metric shows a non-interactive placeholder rather than a misleading zero.

**US-02 — Trend chart**
- Given orders spanning several weeks, when I select weekly granularity, then each bar represents one Monday-starting week and stacks the classifications within it.
- Given a bucket in which a classification has no orders, when the chart renders, then that segment contributes an explicit zero so the stack does not gap.
- Given a range with no orders in an intermediate bucket, when the chart renders, then the empty bucket is still shown (gap-filled) rather than omitted.

**US-03 — Range-scoped pills and drill-through**
- Given I select a 30-day range, when the trend loads, then the range pills summarise the **queried window**, not the first and last bucket boundaries — so the current partial month is not understated.
- Given a range is selected, when I click the "Customer Impacted" pill, then I land on the customer-impacted queue filtered to that date range, with a clearable range chip visible.
- Given the trend request fails, when the pills render, then they show an error state and are not clickable.

**US-05 — Orders grid**
- Given 100k order lines, when I sort or filter, then the query executes server-side and the page returns within the p95 latency NFR.
- Given a filter is active, when I export, then the export reflects the active filter.

**US-06 / US-07 — Order detail and rule trace**
- Given an order has been classified, when I open the Rule Trace tab, then I see every rule evaluated in priority order, whether it matched, and the outcome applied.
- Given a rule references a strategy that is not registered, when the engine evaluates it, then the failure is recorded in the trace as an error and evaluation continues — it must never throw.
- Given no rule matches, when evaluation completes, then the order is classified `INVESTIGATE_REQUIRED` by the priority-1000 catch-all.

**US-08 — CSV import**
- Given a tab-delimited export whose configured delimiter is a comma, when it is imported, then the delimiter is detected from the header and the file imports successfully.
- Given a file whose headers do not fit the source's column mapping, when it is imported, then one actionable error names the missing target fields and quotes the headers actually found.
- Given the same `(order_number, product_code)` arrives again with changed values, when it is imported, then the existing order is updated and a history snapshot of the previous values is written.
- Given a header carries a BOM, zero-width character or non-breaking space, when it is matched, then it normalises to the same key used for row lookup.

**US-11 / US-12 / US-13 — Provisioning failures**
- Given the daily report lists a failure for order number X, when it is imported, then the failure is categorised, an owning team and suggested action are attached, and it is joined to every order line with that order number.
- Given a failure report line is wrapped across fixed-width continuation lines, when it is parsed, then the continuation is rejoined and only recognised labels start a new field.
- Given an order that already exists is newly linked to an unresolved failure, when the import completes, then the affected orders are reclassified so the priority-15 rule takes effect.
- Given a previously reported failure is absent from today's report **and** every line of that report matched, when the import completes, then the failure auto-resolves — but only if the order was imported more recently than the failure was last seen.
- Given a failure that arrived in today's report, when auto-resolve runs, then it is not closed.

**US-15 — Audit**
- Given any create, update, delete, import, resolve or reassign, when it completes, then an audit record is written with actor, action, entity, before/after and timestamp.

**US-17 — Authentication and authorisation** 🔴 *not met in production*
- Given `AUTH_ENABLED=true`, when an unauthenticated request arrives, then it is rejected with 401.
- Given a viewer token, when a state-changing endpoint is called, then it is rejected with 403.
- Given an admin token, when any endpoint is called, then it is permitted (admin ⊃ operator ⊃ viewer).
- **Current production behaviour:** `AUTH_ENABLED=false`; every visitor is treated as an admin.

| Unauthenticated production access | 0 | 🔴 100% — BLK-01 |

### Non-Goals

Order placement, amendment or cancellation (the Control Tower is read-and-annotate, never a
system of record for orders). Writing back to ActiveHub, GPS, Licence Manager or any upstream
system. Customer-facing or partner-facing access. Learner-facing anything. Billing,
entitlement or licence issuance. Automated remediation of provisioning failures. Any AI or ML
inference in the classification path. Multi-tenant isolation. Real-time streaming ingestion
(the model is scheduled/batch import with manual upload). Mobile-native apps. Replacing the
downstream failure email at source.

## 3. Architecture Artefacts

### Current state (as delivered)

```text
Browser (Next.js 15 App Router, MUI v6, TanStack Query, Zustand, Recharts)
   │  HTTPS, JSON
   ▼
NestJS API  (apps/api)  — global prefix /api, URI versioning v1
   ├─ auth        JwtAuthGuard (Entra ID JWKS) + RolesGuard      [flagged off in prod]
   ├─ orders      list / export / detail / trace / history / related / audit / failures / bulk
   ├─ dashboard   summary / by-status / by-product / by-source / trend / health
   ├─ imports     upload / runs
   ├─ sources     CRUD / types / test / run / runs
   ├─ rules       CRUD / strategies / preview / reapply
   ├─ failures    list / breakdown / resolve / reassign / resync
   ├─ audit       query
   ├─ views       saved views
   ├─ aggregates  daily rollups
   └─ health      /healthz /readyz /metrics  (outside the /api prefix)
   │
   ├── in-process typed event bus (@nestjs/event-emitter)
   │     order.imported · order.updated · order.classified · order.reclassified
   │     import.completed · import.failed
   │
   ├── @control-tower/ingestion      connector registry, CSV parser, normaliser,
   │                                 failure-report parser        (no Nest, no Prisma)
   ├── @control-tower/classification rule engine + strategy registry (no Nest, no Prisma)
   ├── @control-tower/reporting      trend bucketing, summaries, operational health
   └── @control-tower/shared-types   enums, DTOs, event names — shared with the web app
   │
   ▼
PostgreSQL 16 via Prisma
   sources · import_runs · orders · order_history · classification_rules ·
   rule_executions · provisioning_failures · audit_logs · saved_views · daily_aggregates
```

Ingress sources: manual CSV upload, CSV file drop, REST API pull, Azure Blob, and the daily
provisioning-failure email report. SFTP, SharePoint and Tableau are registered source types
with connector stubs and are **not implemented**.

### Target state (unratified)

The original intent was Azure App Service / Container Apps with Entra ID enforced. The delivered
system runs on Railway with authentication disabled. That divergence is unresolved and is
recorded as ADR-12 (open) and BLK-01 / BLK-04. The in-process event bus is deliberately a seam:
event names are centralised so the transport can be swapped for Azure Service Bus without
touching publishers or subscribers, and the `services/*` packages carry no framework dependency
so they can be lifted into workers.

### Architecture Decision Records

| ADR | Decision | Status |
|---|---|---|
| ADR-01 | Modular monolith: domain logic lives in dependency-free workspace libraries (`services/ingestion`, `services/classification`, `services/reporting`) consumed by the NestJS API, so it can be split into workers later without a rewrite | ✅ Implemented, unratified |
| ADR-02 | Classification uses the strategy pattern with a registry (`field-match`, `order-age`, `always`); rules are rows in `classification_rules`, evaluated ascending by priority, first match wins, full trace persisted to `rule_executions` | ✅ Implemented, unratified |
| ADR-03 | Ingestion uses the strategy pattern with a connector registry; each connector declares its own capabilities (`supportsScheduledFetch`, `supportsUpload`, `uploadAccept`, `uploadLabel`) and both the UI picker and server-side upload validation are derived from that declaration | ✅ Implemented, unratified |
| ADR-04 | Deduplication on the natural key `(order_number, product_code)`; every overwrite writes an `order_history` snapshot of the previous values | ✅ Implemented, unratified |
| ADR-05 | Orchestration via an in-process typed event bus with centrally declared event names, as a seam for a future Azure Service Bus transport | ✅ Implemented, unratified |
| ADR-06 | The latest unresolved provisioning failure is denormalised onto `orders` (`provisioning_category`, `provisioning_owner`, `provisioning_failed_at`) so queues, filters and the rule engine need no join; `provisioning_failures` remains the record of truth | ✅ Implemented, unratified |
| ADR-07 | The daily failure email is a **snapshot**, not an event stream: absence means resolved. Auto-resolve requires that every line of the report matched **and** the order was imported more recently than the failure was last seen, using `imported_at` rather than `updated_at` because our own summary writes touch `updated_at` | ✅ Implemented, unratified |
| ADR-08 | Ownership routing is a static table (`FAILURE_ROUTING`) applied at import time and **stored on the failure**, so reassignment never rewrites history and changing the table only affects newly imported failures | ✅ Implemented, unratified |
| ADR-09 | Prisma with hand-written SQL migrations; an idempotent seed runs at container boot and also retires superseded rules and sources and migrates legacy column mappings | ✅ Implemented, unratified |
| ADR-10 | Authentication via Entra ID OIDC (JWKS + `passport-jwt`), authorisation via a role hierarchy admin ⊃ operator ⊃ viewer, with an `AUTH_ENABLED=false` bypass intended for local development only | 🔴 Implemented but **disabled in production** — BLK-01 |
| ADR-11 | Next.js 15 App Router with `output: 'standalone'` and `transpilePackages`, MUI v6 + MUI X DataGrid (server-driven), Recharts | ✅ Implemented, unratified |
| ADR-12 | Hosting platform: Railway (delivered) versus Azure App Service / Container Apps (original intent) | 🔴 Open — unresolved contradiction |
| ADR-13 | Container images are not built in CI; only `npm run build` and tests run | 🔴 Open — has caused two production incidents (see §8) |
| ADR-14 | No AI/ML in the classification path; classification is deterministic, inspectable and human-editable | 🟢 Confirmed by omission — record explicitly before any future change |
| ADR-15 | Data residency and hosting region for order and customer data | 🔴 Open — not assessed |

### Non-Functional Requirements

| NFR | Target | Status |
|---|---|---|
| API p95 latency, list endpoints | ≤ 500 ms at 100k order lines | Not load tested |
| Availability | 99.5% | No SLO instrumentation |
| Automated test coverage, new code | ≥ 80% | Enforced only in one package — BLK-08 |
| PII in logs | 0 | No automated scan — BLK-09 |
| Accessibility | WCAG 2.2 AA | Never audited — BLK-06 |
| Security baseline | OWASP ASVS L2 | Partial: helmet, CORS allowlist, global validation pipe with `forbidNonWhitelisted`, Prisma parameterisation, RBAC. **Authentication not enforced** — BLK-01 |
| Audit coverage of state changes | 100% | Implemented; not sampled or evidenced |
| Import determinism | Same file imported twice produces no duplicate order lines | Covered by tests |
| Rule engine resilience | An unknown or failing strategy is traced, never thrown | Covered by tests |
| Observability | Structured JSON logs with correlation IDs, `/healthz`, `/readyz`, Prometheus `/metrics`, opt-in OpenTelemetry | Implemented |
| Data residency | 🔴 TBD | Not assessed — ADR-15 |
| Backup and restore | 🔴 TBD | Not documented or tested — BLK-11 |

### Architecture risks

1. **The event bus is in-process.** A crash between "order imported" and "order classified"
   leaves the order unclassified until the next reapply. There is no outbox and no retry.
2. **Denormalised provisioning summary can drift** from `provisioning_failures` if a write path
   bypasses `syncOrderSummaries()`. `POST /failures/resync` exists as the repair, but drift is
   not detected automatically.
3. **Seed-at-boot mutates production data** (retiring rules, migrating mappings). It is
   idempotent and tested, but it is a write path that runs without a human in the loop.
4. **No tenancy model.** The schema assumes one operating unit.
5. **Scientific-notation ISBNs** arriving from the ActiveHub export (`9.78141E+12`) are
   unrecoverable in code; the fix must be made at source by formatting the column as Text.

### Coding standards and AI coding controls

- TypeScript strict; no `any` in new code.
- Domain logic belongs in `services/*` — dependency-free and testable without a database.
  Nest modules orchestrate; they do not hold business rules.
- Every defect fix ships with a regression test that fails before the fix.
- Error messages must be actionable and must quote the offending input, not blame the user.
- British English in user-facing copy.
- `apps/api/tsconfig.build.json` pins `rootDir: "src"` and excludes `prisma`. **Do not remove
  this** — without it, adding a file outside `src/` silently moves the emitted entrypoint from
  `dist/main.js` to `dist/src/main.js` and the container crash-loops while `npm run build`
  reports success. The Dockerfile's `test -f` guards exist for the same reason.
- The full AI coding control set is the banner at the top of this document and
  `guardrails` in the companion manifest.

### Coverage model

Target ≥ 80% for new code. Currently enforced by a `coverageThreshold` only in
`services/classification`; every other workspace reports coverage without failing the build.
Closing this is ENG-705 / BLK-08.

### Representative BDD scenarios already covered by tests

- Delimiter detection: a tab-delimited file with a comma configured imports successfully.
- Header normalisation: BOM, zero-width and non-breaking-space headers resolve to the same key
  used for row lookup, so the header check and the row read cannot disagree.
- Mapping mismatch: an unfitting file yields one actionable error naming the missing targets and
  quoting the headers found.
- Dedup: re-importing the same `(orderNumber, productCode)` updates in place and snapshots history.
- Rule engine: unknown strategy is traced as an error and evaluation continues.
- Rule engine: no match falls through to the priority-1000 catch-all.
- Completed reconciliation: `COMPLETED` requires **both** licence match flags to read `Match`.
- Failure parsing: fixed-width continuation lines are rejoined, and only recognised labels start
  a new field, so `GPS-invokeCreateGPSApi:HTTP/1.1 400` inside a continuation is not read as one.
- Failure categorisation: most-specific matcher wins.
- Auto-resolve: a failure reported today is never closed by the same import.
- Auto-resolve: closure requires that every report line matched.
- Late-arriving orders: importing orders re-links and reclassifies against open failures.
- `includeResolved=false` excludes resolved failures (explicit boolean transform, not `Boolean('false')`).
- Trend summary: the total comes from each bucket's own total, because unclassified orders
  belong in the total but have no classification bucket.
- Upload validation: an extension the connector does not declare is rejected server-side.

### Test gaps (release-blocking)

| Gap | Task |
|---|---|
| No container image build or boot test | ENG-704 |
| No accessibility tests, automated or manual | ENG-707 / ENG-708 |
| No load or soak test against the p95 NFR | ENG-715 |
| No security testing: no dependency scan, no secret scan, no threat model | ENG-711 / ENG-712 |
| No coverage gate outside one package | ENG-705 |
| No test that authentication is enforced when `AUTH_ENABLED=true` in a deployed environment | ENG-701 |
| No restore test | ENG-709 |

### Defect severity model

| Severity | Definition | Response |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Data loss, unauthorised access, PII exposure, or the platform is down | Stop the line; rollback |
| S2 | Orders misclassified, imports silently dropping rows, failures not routed | Fix before next import cycle |
| S3 | A view is wrong or degraded but the data is correct | Next iteration |
| S4 | Cosmetic | Backlog |

Release-blocking categories: any open S1; any S2 affecting classification correctness,
deduplication or the audit path.

## 6. DevOps & Operations Artefacts

### Environments

| Environment | Status |
|---|---|
| Local (Docker Compose: Postgres + api + web) | ✅ |
| CI (GitHub Actions, Postgres service container) | ✅ |
| Production (Railway: Postgres + api + web, both tracking `main`) | ✅ Live |
| Staging / pre-production | 🔴 Does not exist — changes go from CI to production |

### CI/CD

Current pipeline (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), on pull request and on push to `main`:
install → `prisma generate` → `npm run build` → `npm test` → `prisma migrate deploy` → API e2e.

Railway builds the container images itself on push to `main` and runs migrations and the
idempotent seed at container boot.

**Gap:** CI never builds a container image. Two production-affecting defects have reached
`main` through that gap — a mis-rooted API build output (`dist/src/main.js` vs `dist/main.js`)
and a web image missing `services/reporting`, where npm created a dangling symlink and exited 0.
Both passed `npm run build` and every test. ENG-704 / BLK-05.

### Release strategy

Trunk-based: branch, pull request, human review, squash to `main`, Railway redeploys.
No feature flags exist for user-visible change — the platform is small and single-tenant and
change has so far been shipped whole. This is a divergence from the Pearson guardrail requiring
feature flags for user-visible change and is recorded as exception candidate EXC-01.

### Rollback

Redeploy the previous Railway deployment. **Migrations are not reversible** — there are no down
migrations, so a rollback across a schema change is not currently safe. ENG-709 and a down-
migration policy are prerequisites for a credible rollback plan.

### Observability

Available: structured JSON logs with correlation IDs, `/healthz`, `/readyz`, Prometheus
`/metrics`, opt-in OpenTelemetry, an `ErrorTrackingService` seam, and the in-app operational
health view (`GET /api/v1/dashboard/health`).

Not yet in place: dashboards, alert routing, an on-call rota, or any SLO.

### Alerts required before release-ready

| Severity | Alert |
|---|---|
| S1 | API unavailable / readiness failing |
| S1 | Database unreachable |
| S1 | Any PII detected in logs |
| S1 | Unauthenticated access succeeding once `AUTH_ENABLED=true` |
| S2 | Import run failed, or completed with errors above threshold |
| S2 | Scheduled source has not run within its cron window |
| S2 | Orders left unclassified after an import cycle |
| S2 | Catch-all rule share above 5% of a run |
| S3 | Provisioning failures unresolved beyond SLA by owning team |
| S3 | Latency p95 breach |

### Runbooks required (none authored yet — ENG-710)

| ID | Runbook |
|---|---|
| RB-01 | API or web service down |
| RB-02 | Database unreachable or out of connections |
| RB-03 | Import run failed — triage and safe re-run |
| RB-04 | Import imported the wrong data — how to correct without losing history |
| RB-05 | Column mapping no longer fits the upstream export |
| RB-06 | Provisioning failure report format changed |
| RB-07 | Orders stuck unclassified — reapply rules safely |
| RB-08 | Provisioning summary drifted from `provisioning_failures` — resync |
| RB-09 | Rollback a deployment (including the migration caveat) |
| RB-10 | Database backup and point-in-time restore |
| RB-11 | Rotate database and Entra ID secrets |
| RB-12 | Suspected PII in logs |
| RB-13 | Suspected unauthorised access |
| RB-14 | Subject rights request touching imported customer data |
| RB-15 | Emergency disable of a data source |

### Support model

🔴 TBD. No named service owner, no on-call, no support hours, no incident process.

## 8. Consolidated Warnings & Open Items

### Certification blockers

| ID | Blocker | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| BLK-01 | `AUTH_ENABLED=false` in production — the platform is publicly reachable and every visitor is treated as an admin, over data that includes customer names and email addresses | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-02 | POLARIS Data Privacy Review not performed; personal data is in scope | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-03 | Portfolio Reuse Review not performed against ActiveHub, GPS, Licence Manager, PRIZM, OneCRM | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-04 | Target architecture unresolved: Azure (intended) versus Railway (delivered) | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-05 | CI does not build container images; two production incidents have reached `main` through this gap | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-06 | No accessibility audit — WCAG 2.2 AA is claimed as an NFR and has never been verified | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-07 | No named owners for Product, Technical, Business, Architecture, Privacy or Security | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-08 | Coverage floor of 80% is not enforced outside `services/classification` | 🟠 Material |
| BLK-09 | No PII-in-logs scan | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-10 | No retention schedule or deletion job for imported customer data | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-11 | Backup and restore neither documented nor tested; no down migrations, so rollback across a schema change is unsafe | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-12 | No threat model, dependency scan or secret scan; file upload is an unmodelled untrusted input boundary | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-13 | Data residency not assessed | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-14 | No staging environment — changes go from CI to production | 🟠 Material |
| BLK-15 | No runbooks, alerts, SLOs, on-call or named service owner | 🔴 Critical |
| BLK-16 | Delivery preceded specification: ADRs are implemented but unratified, and no review gate has been passed | 🔴 Critical |

### Warnings

1. Seed-at-boot mutates production data (retires rules and sources, migrates legacy mappings).
   Idempotent and tested, but unattended.
2. The in-process event bus has no outbox and no retry; a crash between import and classify
   leaves orders unclassified until a manual reapply.
3. `orders.provisioning_*` can drift from `provisioning_failures` if a write path bypasses
   `syncOrderSummaries()`; drift is repairable but not detected.
4. Nest 11 emits an `/api/*` route-pattern deprecation warning.
5. The ActiveHub export delivers ISBNs in scientific notation (`9.78141E+12`); the source column
   must be formatted as Text — no code fix is possible.
6. Success measures in §2 are largely uninstrumented, so improvement over Excel cannot be evidenced.
7. Rules are editable by admins at runtime with no approval step; a bad rule reclassifies the
   whole estate on reapply.
8. No feature flags, so user-visible change ships whole (see EXC-01).

## 9. Next Steps (offline, human)

1. **Close BLK-01 first.** Enable Entra ID in production and put the authenticated principal in
   the audit trail (ENG-701 … ENG-703). Everything else is secondary to a public, unauthenticated
   surface over customer data.
2. Name the owners (ENG-B03) — nine of the open questions cannot be answered without them.
3. Run the Portfolio Reuse Review (ENG-B01) and the POLARIS Data Privacy Review (ENG-B02).
4. Close ADR-12 (hosting) and ADR-15 (residency); ratify ADR-01 … ADR-11 as written.
5. Add the container image build to CI (ENG-704) — the single highest-value pipeline change,
   on the evidence of two incidents.
6. Add the coverage gate, PII-in-logs scan and `axe` checks (ENG-705 … ENG-707).
7. Document and test backup and restore, and adopt a down-migration policy (ENG-709).
8. Author the 15 runbooks and stand up alerting (ENG-710, ENG-714).
9. Commission the WCAG 2.2 AA audit (ENG-708).
10. Instrument the success measures so the Excel-replacement claim can be evidenced (ENG-715).
11. Submit OCT-001 for human certification once P0 and P7 are closed.
